questions.question: When are the kharif crops harvested?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**September - October**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The crops which are sown in the rainy season are called Kharif crops.
 
• Kharif crops are the crops that are sown at the beginning of the rainy season, e.g. between April and May. 
 
• The Kharif crops are harvested in the month of September-October
 
• Important crops grown during this season are paddy, maize, jowar, bajra, tur (arhar), moong, urad, cotton, jute, groundnut and soybean.
 
• Kharif crop requires high temperature and high humidity.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are three cropping seasons in India.
 
 
• Rabi.
 
• Kharif.
 
• Zaid.
 
 
 
• Rabi crops are sown in the winter season from October to December and harvested in the summer season from April to June.
 
 
• Wheat, Barley, Peas, Gram, and Mustard-produced during Rabi.
 
 
 
• Zaid season is a short season In between the Rabi and the Kharif seasons.
 
 
• Cucumber and watermelon are produced during Zaid.

questions.question: What type of the rock is Granite?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Intrusive igneous rocks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__**Concept: **__

__
 
• A **rock** is any **naturally occurring solid mass or aggregate of one or more minerals** or mineraloid matter.
 
• The earth's **crust is composed of rocks.**
 
• It is categorized by the **minerals included its chemical composition **and the way in which it is formed.
 
• The rock cycle is a basic concept of transitions through geologic time among the three main rock types: **sedimentary, metamorphic, and igneous.**
 
• Each rock type is altered when it is forced out of its equilibrium conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Types of rocks**
 **Characteristics**
 
 

 **Igneous rock**
 
 
 
• It is formed when **molten rock (magma or lava) cools and solidifies.**
 
• Igneous rock may form with or without crystallization.
 
• It may be intrusive (plutonic) rocks or extrusive (volcanic) rocks.
 
• For example, **Granite, Basalt, etc.**
 

 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/974568e7db83f818a3567f7d2a635639513f30755928fc08e28ffed00807654f.png] ​

 
 
 

 **Sedimentary rock**
 
 
 
• They originate when **particles settle out of water or air, or by precipitation** of minerals from water.
 
• They accumulate in layers.
 
• For example, **Sandstone, Limestone, etc.**
 

 
**​** [IMAGE: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/Triassic_Utah.JPG/400px-Triassic_Utah.JPG] 

 
 
 

 **Metamorphic rock**
 
 
 
• They are formed when existing rocks are **changed by heat, pressure, or reactive fluids,** such as hot, mineral-laden water.
 
• For example, **Marble, Quartzite, Schist, etc.**
 

 
**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5beed19d56e85eabea71756d56469d93ed540284b346ff5f9075fbd3b5675f41.png]

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Metals react with acids and produce metal salts and hydrogen gas.
Non-metals react with oxygen to produce non- metallic oxides which are basic in nature.
On burning, metals react with oxygen to produce metal oxides which are acidic in nature.
Less reactive metals displace more reactive metals from their compounds in aqueous solutions.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Metals react with acids and produce metal salts and hydrogen gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an acid reacts with metal, salt and hydrogen are produced:
 
 
• Acid + Metal → Salt + Hydrogen
 
• An example: Nitric acid + Calcium → Nitrate + Hydrogen.
 
• The salt that is produced depends upon which acid and which metal react.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Metals readily react with acid and produce hydrogen gas which burns with a pop sound.
 
• Metals are placed above hydrogen in reactivity series and displace during a reaction with an acid.
 
• As acids have a property of giving H+ ions.
 
• A resultant is formed with the release of hydrogen gas. 
 
• It doesn't matter which metal or which acid is used if there is a reaction we always get hydrogen gas as well as salt.
 
• However, how quickly the reaction goes depends on the metal used and how high up in the reactivity series it is.

• The Caste Disabilities Removal Act, 1850, was a law passed in British India under East India Company rule, that abolished all laws affecting the rights of people converting to another religion or caste.

questions.question: The potential difference, V, across the ends of a given metallic wire in an electric circuit is directly proportional to the current flowing through it, provided its temperature remains the same. This is called ______ law.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Ohm's**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The relationship between current, voltage, and resistance is described by Ohm's law. This law is given by George Simon Ohm in 1828

Ohm’s law:__

__
 
• Ohm’s law states that at a constant temperature, the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• Voltage = Current × Resistance
 
 
• V = I × R
 
• V = voltage, I = current and R = resistance
 
 
 
• The SI unit of resistance is ohms and is denoted by Ω.
 
• It helps to calculate the power, efficiency, current, voltage, and resistance of an element of an electrical circuit.
 
• If an element follows ohm’s law, then the element is known as a linear element.
 
• Ex: Resistor

Limitation of ohm's Law:__

__
 
• Ohm’s law is applicable for conductors only.
 
• Ohm’s law does not apply to unilateral networks. Unilateral networks allow the current to flow in one direction. Such types of networks consist of elements like a diode, transistor, etc.
 
• Ohm’s law is also not applicable to non - linear elements.
 
• Non-linear elements are those which do not have current exactly proportional to the applied voltage that means the resistance value of those elements changes for different values of voltage and current. An example of a non-linear element is a thyristor.
 
• Ohm’s law is also not applicable to vacuum tubes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Boyle’s Law**

 
• ​Boyle's law is a gas law that states that a gas's pressure and volume are inversely proportional.
 
• It states that at a constant temperature, the pressure exerted by a gas is inversely proportional to the volume occupied by it.
 
• According to the Boyle's Law:
 
 
• P1V1 = P2V2
 
 
• Where P1 = Initial Pressure

 P2 = Final Pressure

 V1 = Initial Volume 

 V2 = Final Volume

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/883ca4a9c62fe7d942ab5573518c8cee4603dd50fc0953b220b928a0f514f177.png] 
 
 
 
 

The five main gas laws in chemistry are Boyle's Law, Charle's Law, Gay Lussac's Law, Avogadro's Law, and Ideal Gas Law.

 
• Charle's law states that the volume of an ideal gas is directly proportional to the absolute temperature at constant pressure.
 
• Gay-Lussac's law states that the pressure of a given mass of gas varies directly with the absolute temperature of the gas when the volume is kept constant.
 
• Avogadro's law or Avogadro-Ampère's hypothesis is an experimental gas law relating the volume of a gas to the amount of substance of gas present.
 
• The ideal gas law states that the product of the pressure and the volume of one gram molecule of an ideal gas is equal to the product of the absolute temperature of the gas and the universal gas constant.

questions.question: In ______, the British government enacted a legislation banning the use of printed cotton textiles - chintz - in England. Interestingly, this Act was known as the Calico Act.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1720**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1720**, the British government **enacted legislation known as the Calico Act, banning the use of printed cotton textiles - chintz - in England.**
 
• This Act was brought into effect due to the fear that the import of** cheap, colourful, and washable Indian textiles was harming the British wool and silk industries, **which were unable to compete with the more attractive Indian products.
 
• The Calico Act prohibited the use of Indian textiles in Britain, **but they were still allowed for re-export to other places, which ensured the continued operation of the East India Company.**
 
• **The Act illustrates the early impact of global trade and market forces and the measures that governments took to protect their domestic industries.**
 
• Over time, as Britain's own cotton industry developed, the restrictions imposed by the** Calico Act were gradually lifted.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calico Act:**

 
 
• The** Calico Act of 1720 **was a piece of protectionist legislation by the British government.
 
• **Calico refers to unbleached, plain-woven cotton textiles, initially imported from India.**
 
• The use of calico from India had become widespread in **England since it was inexpensive, brightly coloured, and considered exotic.**
 
• **The British textile industry felt threatened by the importation of Indian calico.**
 
• To protect its wool and silk industries, the government passed the **Calico Act, banning the use of cotton textiles in England.**
 
• **The Act is a significant indicator of how the British used legislation to control markets and trade in the interests of their home industries.**

questions.question: In which of the following modes of data transmission, can the data flow in both directions simultaneously?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Full-duplex**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Full-duplex mode refers to the method of data transmission in which data can flow in both directions simultaneously.
 
• In this mode, both the sender and receiver can transmit data at the same time.
 
• This is akin to a telephone conversation where both parties can talk and listen simultaneously.
 
• Full-duplex communication requires two independent channels, one for sending data and the other for receiving.
 
• This mode is more efficient than half-duplex and simplex modes as it allows communication in both directions at the same time, making it faster for large amounts of data.
 
• Full-duplex systems are used in situations where there is a large volume of data to be transmitted and there is a need for real-time communication, such as in video conferencing, telephony, and server-client communication.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Simplex
 
 
In the simplex mode of communication, the data flows in only one direction, from the sender to the receiver.

 
A good example of this mode is a keyboard or a mouse where input devices send data to the computer and there is no data sent back from the computer to these devices.

 
 
 

 Quarter-duplex
 
 
Quarter-duplex is not a standard mode of data transmission.

 
The standard modes are simplex, half-duplex, and full-duplex.

 
 
 

 Half-duplex
 
 
In half-duplex mode, data can be sent in both directions, but not at the same time.

 
When one device is sending, the other can only receive, and vice versa.

 
Walkie-talkies are a good example of devices operating in half-duplex mode.

questions.question: Which of the following shortcut key is used to copy the selected data in MS-Word 365?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ctrl + C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ctrl + C **is a universal keyboard shortcut on Microsoft systems that copies the selected text or item to the clipboard.
 
• **This shortcut is used across many applications, not just MS Word.**
 
• This includes other** Microsoft Office applications, browsers, and file explorer.**
 
• The copied data can then be pasted elsewhere using the keyboard shortcut **Ctrl + V.**
 
• This is a quicker and more efficient way of copying data than using the mouse to select** 'Copy' from the right-click context menu or from the 'Edit' menu in the toolbar.**
 
• It's also worth noting that the original data remains in place after the copy operation, allowing it to be copied to multiple locations if desired.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Shortcut Key
 Function

questions.question: Which of the following states has Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation Limited?

__
 
• **Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation Limited is situated in Karnataka,** a state in the southwestern region of India.
 
• This Corporation was established for the upliftment of the** Scheduled Tribes in the state of Karnataka.**
 
• It aims to **provide financial assistance for income-generating activities to Scheduled Tribes in the state, contributing to their economic development.**
 
• The Corporation also organizes awareness and training programs to help **Scheduled Tribes members become self-sufficient.**
 
• Besides providing financial aid, the **Corporation's functions also include offering educational assistance, conducting surveys for need-based programs, and facilitating employment-oriented training programs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Maharshi Valmiki:**

 
 
• Maharshi Valmiki is revered as the first poet of Sanskrit literature.
 
• **He is the author of the epic Ramayana, which narrates the life of Lord Rama.**
 
• Valmiki's contributions to Indian literature are highly esteemed, and he holds a significant place in the cultural and religious history of India.
 
• His name is often associated with social justice initiatives in** India, symbolizing upliftment and empowerment, especially in the context of organizations like Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation Limited.**
 
 
 
• **Apart from the Ramayana, there are other works attributed to Valmiki in traditional Indian literature.**
 
• However, it's worth noting that the authorship of these works is often disputed due to the time elapsed since they were written.
 
• **These works include:**__

 
• **Yoga Vasistha:**

 
 
• Sometimes attributed to** Valmiki, this is a discourse by sage Vasistha to Prince Rama, during a period when Rama is in a dejected state.**
 
• **It contains teachings of Advaita Vedanta and is structured as a conversation between Vasistha, a learned sage, and Rama.**
 
 
 
• **Valmiki Ramayana in Prakrit:**
 
 
• This is said to be a version of the Ramayana written by** Valmiki in Prakrit language, but its authenticity and authorship are debated among scholars.**

questions.question: An image formed by the convex mirror is always ______.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is virtual and erect.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Convex Mirror**

 
 
• A Convex Mirror curves outward like the back of a spoon.
 
• In a convex mirror, light originating from the same point will reflect off the mirror surface and diverge.
 
• Hence convex mirror is sometimes referred to as a diverging mirror.
 
• The type of image formed by these mirrors is always imaginary or virtual.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Convex Mirror**
 
 
• It is used as a rearview mirror in the vehicle because it provides the maximum near field of view.
 
• In Sodium reflector lamp.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fbda5549e3712d52ce25b97ce715b80f4bbcbebb25901abe4074063513ecbb81.png] 

 
• **Concave Mirror**

 
 
• A Concave mirror is a mirror that has a slightly inward curve like the inside of a spoon.
 
• The Curved surfaces focus parallel rays from a great distance into a single point for enhanced intensity.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Concave Mirror**
 
 
• As a shaving glass
 
• As a reflector for headlights of vehicles, and searchlights.
 
• An ophthalmoscope examines the eye, ear, and nose doctors.
 
• In Solar cookers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fbfc7119d307ac7c8645b7aa8b6088a79bdc77c3302fff3bbf5a56decade3ff7.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• Do not confuse between Concave/Convex Lens and Mirror
 
• **Convex lens**
 
 
• The convex lens is also called a converging lens.
 
 
 
• **Concave lens**
 
 
• The concave lens is also called a diverging lens.

questions.question: The production function can be expressed as _______. (where L is labour and C is capital and Q is the maximum output that can be produced)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Q = f(L, C)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The production function is a mathematical** representation of the relationship between inputs (like labour and capital) and the output of a firm or industry.**
 
• The production function typically takes the form
 
 
• **Q = f(L, C)**
 
• **Where Q represents the maximum output that can be produced given the inputs.**
 
• In this equation, L is the quantity of labor used in the production process and C is the quantity of capital used.
 
• The function f(.) describes the specific relationship between the inputs and output.
 
 
 
• This relationship is usually determined empirically, based on observations of real-world production processes.
 
• The equation **Q = f(L, C) is a representation of the concept of production technology, which describes how firms transform inputs into outputs.**
 
• **It's a fundamental concept in the study of production and cost in microeconomics.**

questions.question: Central Bureau of Intelligence and Investigation comes under which list of the seventh schedule of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Union list**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Central Bureau of Intelligence and Investigation (CBI)** comes under the **Union List of the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.**
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution is about the allocation of powers and functions between the Union and the States.
 
• **It contains three lists:**
 
 
• **Union List**
 
• **State List, and**
 
• **Concurrent List.**
 
 
 
• The Union List is where the **Union has exclusive powers to deal with certain subjects.**
 
• The **Central Bureau of Intelligence and Investigation is one of the subjects in the Union List.**
 
• This means that the central government has exclusive jurisdiction over the **CBI**, which is a key agency for national intelligence and investigations​1​.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **State List:**

 
 
• This list contains subjects on which only the state government can make laws.
 
• The subjects under this list pertain to matters of regional and local importance.
 
• **Examples include police, agriculture, and public health.**
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List:**
 
 
• **​**This list contains subjects on which both the Union and the State Governments are competent to legislate.
 
• However, in case of a conflict between Union and State law on the same subject, the Union law prevails.
 
• **Examples of subjects in this list include bankruptcy and insolvency, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy and insolvency, and education.**
 
 
 
• **Transferred List:**
 
 
• This option is not a part of the **Seventh Schedule.**
 
• It might be a reference to the subjects that were transferred from the** State List to the Concurrent List by constitutional amendments, but it's not an official term used in the Indian Constitution.**
 
 

2f:T
